jobs.title: Backend Developer
jobs.descriptionHtml:
We’re looking for a Backend Developer to design and build the services at the core of Bay Cloud. That covers everything from ingesting agent activity at scale to the risk scoring and policy compilation behind every Allow, Ask, Deny or Steer decision. You’ll join a small, senior R&D team in Tel Aviv that ships to production daily and treats AI tools as a core part of how it works.

What you’ll do

  • Design, build and own the backend services behind Bay Cloud: APIs, data models and the business logic that powers the platform.

  • Build the pipelines that ingest millions of events from devices, browsers and cloud workloads, normalize them and turn them into an entity graph, activity timelines and findings.

  • Develop the services that score risk continuously and compile policies per device and agent, so enforcement decisions happen in milliseconds.

  • Own reliability and scale, from performance and observability to testing, code reviews and production support.

  • Work directly with product, frontend and customers to shape what we build next, and help set our architecture as we grow.

What we’re looking for

  • 5+ years of hands-on backend development, building and owning services in production.

  • Heavy, hands-on use of AI coding tools, with automation built into how you work.

  • Strong TypeScript and Node.js, or another modern backend language such as Go or Python.

  • Deep experience with PostgreSQL, data modeling and API design (REST or GraphQL).

  • Experience building distributed, cloud-native systems on AWS, with containers and Kubernetes.

  • A builder’s mindset: you take a vague problem, break it down and deliver at startup pace.

  • Strong communication in English and Hebrew.

Nice to have

  • Background in cybersecurity products (endpoint, API, cloud or identity security).

  • Experience with event streaming and queues (Kafka, SQS or similar), high-scale data processing or graph databases.

  • Experience from an elite technology unit (8200, Mamram or similar), or a B.Sc. in Computer Science or equivalent experience.

Why join Bay

  • Build a new category of AI agent security from the ground floor, with enterprise customers including Micron Technology, Peloton and ClickUp already live.

  • High ownership: your code reaches customers within days, not quarters.

  • Work with a senior team of engineers who have built and scaled security products before.

  • Competitive salary and meaningful equity in a well-funded, Series A stage company.

jobs.title: Senior BDR - EMEA
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Bay

AI agents now write code, run commands and touch company data on every laptop. Bay is building the security layer that lets enterprises adopt them without losing control.

Bay is an agentic endpoint security platform. It discovers every AI agent, MCP server, IDE and browser extension across a company's endpoints, separates human activity from agent activity, and enforces real-time guardrails on what agents can do - with no persistent agent to install.

  • See it: a live entity graph of every user, agent, permission and credential across the fleet.

  • Know it: prompt-to-action attribution, activity timelines and continuous risk scoring.

  • Control it: a deterministic policy engine that returns Allow, Ask or Deny on the device in milliseconds.

Founded in 2025 and headquartered in Tel Aviv, Bay is led by Yuval Zacharia (CEO), Aner Morag (CPO) and Boris Danilovich (VP Engineering). Our engineers come from Mamram, Noname Security (acquired by Akamai), Waycare and other top Israeli cyber companies, and we already protect enterprise customers in the US.

The role

We're looking for a senior Business Development Representative to open doors for Bay at EMEA enterprises. You'll own top-of-funnel for a new category - security for AI agents - building strong outbound pipeline with CISOs and security leaders and setting up the first meetings for our Account Executives. You'll be one of our first BDRs in the EMEA, working closely with sales, marketing and the founders, and you'll help shape our outbound playbook from the ground up.

What you'll do

  • Generate qualified pipeline through multi-channel outbound: email, phone, LinkedIn and events.

  • Research target accounts and personas, and build personalized sequences that get CISOs and security leaders to take a first meeting.

  • Qualify inbound and outbound leads, and book meetings that turn into real opportunities for our Account Executives.

  • Experiment with messaging, channels and AI-powered prospecting tools, and share what works with the team.

  • Bring market feedback to sales, marketing and product, and help build our outbound playbook and process.

What we're looking for

  • 3+ years as a BDR or SDR in B2B enterprise sales, with at least 2 years selling cybersecurity solutions.

  • A consistent track record of meeting and exceeding meeting and pipeline targets.

  • Experience at early-stage or growth-stage startups, ideally Israeli cyber startups.

  • Proven ability to build strong outbound pipeline from scratch, without relying on inbound leads.

  • Hands-on with prospecting and sales tools such as HubSpot or Salesforce, LinkedIn Sales Navigator, Apollo or Outreach, and AI tools for research and personalization.

  • Hungry, resilient and self-driven: you love the hunt, handle rejection well and keep raising the bar.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication, and the confidence to start a conversation with senior security executives.

Nice to have

  • Experience prospecting into endpoint, identity, cloud or AI security buyers.

  • Familiarity with the CISO and security leadership landscape in EMEA enterprises.

  • Experience as one of the first BDRs at a startup, helping build the outbound motion.

Why join Bay

  • Sell a new category - security for the agentic era - at the moment every enterprise is deciding how to adopt AI agents.

  • Get in early: real enterprise customers are already live, and you'll shape how Bay builds pipeline in EMEA.

  • A clear path to grow into an Account Executive role as the team scales.

Location: EMEA, remote

The role

We're looking for a senior Sales Engineer to be the technical lead in Bay's enterprise deals in EMEA. You'll partner with our Account Executives to win over CISOs and security teams, run proofs of value from start to finish and turn early customers into reference accounts. You'll be one of our first SEs in the market, working closely with the founders, product and R&D, and you'll help build how we sell technically from the ground up.

What you'll do

  • Partner with Account Executives across the full sales cycle: discovery, technical qualification, demos and closing.

  • Run proofs of value end to end: scope success criteria, deploy Bay in customer environments, and show results with the customer's own agents, endpoints and policies.

  • Act as a trusted advisor to CISOs, security architects and practitioners on securing AI agents, MCP servers and developer tools.

  • Build demos, POV playbooks, integrations and technical content, using AI tools to automate and scale your work.

  • Bring customer and field feedback to product and R&D, and help shape the roadmap and our technical sales process.

What we're looking for

  • 7+ years in technical customer-facing roles, with at least 4 years as a Sales Engineer or Solution Engineer in cybersecurity.

  • Intensive, hands-on use of AI tools in your daily work - coding assistants, agents and automation - and a deep understanding of how they work.

  • Experience at early-stage or growth-stage startups, ideally Israeli cyber startups, where you built the SE function rather than inherited it.

  • Strong technical depth in endpoint security, identity, cloud security (AWS, Azure, GCP) or developer environments.

  • Hands-on with scripting and APIs (Python, Bash or similar), and comfortable deploying and troubleshooting in enterprise environments.

  • A proven track record of winning complex enterprise POVs and helping close large deals.

  • Excellent communication and presentation skills, from executive briefings to deep technical sessions, and willingness to travel to customers and events.

Nice to have

  • Experience with AI security, MCP or agentic frameworks.

  • Experience with EDR, MDM or endpoint management tools, or integrations with SIEM, SOAR and identity providers.

Why join Bay

  • Work at the forefront of AI: you'll be the expert customers rely on to understand and secure AI agents.

  • Get in early: real enterprise customers are already live, and you'll shape how Bay sells and deploys in EMEA.

  • Work directly with founders and a senior team that has built and scaled security companies before.

Location: EMEA, remote, with travel to customers and events.

jobs.title: Security Researcher
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Bay

AI agents now write code, run commands and touch company data on employee laptops, in the browser, and in cloud sandboxes they spin up on demand. Bay is building the security layer that lets enterprises adopt them without losing control.

Bay is an agentic security platform. It discovers every AI agent, MCP server, IDE and browser extension across a company's endpoints and the cloud environments they connect to. It separates human activity from agent activity and enforces real-time guardrails on what agents can do, with no persistent agent to install.

Founded in 2025 by Yuval Zacharia (CEO), Aner Morag (CPO) and Boris Danilovich (VP Engineering), Bay has R&D in Tel Aviv and a growing go-to-market team in the US and Europe. Our team comes from Noname Security (acquired by Akamai), SentinelOne, Unit 8200, Mamram and other leading cyber companies, and we already protect enterprise customers in the US.

The role

We're hiring a Security Researcher to take apart the AI agents enterprises are adopting, find where they break, and work out how to control them.

Today's agents rarely live in one place. A desktop or browser client sits on the endpoint, the model runs in the vendor's cloud, and the work often happens in a remote VM or container. For each agent, you'll map that chain: where actions execute, how commands travel, who is authenticated, and where we can observe or block. Sometimes the answer looks like offense, such as injecting into a process or speaking an agent's internal protocol, because that's where an enforcement point belongs.

You'll be part of a research group we're building from scratch, working with our Head of Research, detection engineers and R&D. We want every project to do two things: make Bay's product better, and produce something worth publishing.

What you'll do

  • Research AI agents end to end: coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot), cloud and computer-use agents, browser agents and extensions, and MCP servers, across the local client, the cloud control plane and the remote runtime.

  • Reverse engineer clients, runtimes and protocols (Electron/Node apps, native and Rust binaries, sandboxed VMs and containers) on macOS, Windows and Linux to find where agent actions can be observed, intercepted or blocked.

  • Hunt for vulnerabilities in high-impact agent products, such as sandbox and container escapes, cross-tenant access, credential exposure, prompt-injection-to-execution chains, and tool or MCP abuse. Take them through responsible disclosure.

  • Turn findings into product: interception points, enforcement primitives and threat insight that R&D and our detection engineers build into Bay.

  • Build research tooling and PoCs, using AI agents as research partners (LLM-driven Frida, IDA or Ghidra over MCP) to move faster.

  • Track new agent releases, agentic threats, and malicious packages, skills and extensions in the wild.

  • Publish blogs, CVEs, talks and open-source tools that build Bay's voice in the community.

  • Red-team Bay's own guardrails as the team grows.

What we're looking for

  • A track record of original security research: vulnerabilities you found, disclosed or exploited (CVEs, bug bounty, vendor or red-team research). Usually 3+ years, but we care more about what you found than how long it took.

  • Hands-on black-box research: dynamic instrumentation (Frida or similar), traffic interception and TLS decryption, and protocol analysis when you only have the client or only the server.

  • Reverse engineering with IDA, Ghidra, Binary Ninja or similar, including stripped binaries, certificate pinning and custom transports.

  • Strong OS internals: processes, IPC, sandboxing (namespaces, seccomp, micro-VMs) and networking. macOS is a plus.

  • Strong coding in Python plus at least one of TypeScript/JavaScript, Go, Rust or C/C++. You build your own tools.

  • Fluency with AI agents as research tools, and the judgment to check what they tell you.

  • A nose for impact: you pick targets that matter, know when to push harder and when to move on, and work independently from question to result.

  • Evidence discipline: you keep what you observed and reproduced separate from what you inferred.

Nice to have

  • Research on LLM or AI security, prompt injection, agent sandboxes or software supply chain.

  • Cloud and container security: Kubernetes, container runtimes, cloud identity.

  • Published research, conference talks or open-source tools.

  • Background in an IDF technology or intelligence unit (8200, 81, Mamram, Sapir or similar).

  • Exposure to detection engineering or threat hunting.

  • B.Sc. in Computer Science, Mathematics or a related field.

jobs.title: Account Executive
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Bay

AI agents now write code, run commands and touch company data on every laptop. Bay is building the security layer that lets enterprises adopt them without losing control.

Bay is an agentic endpoint security platform. It discovers every AI agent, MCP server, IDE and browser extension across a company's endpoints, separates human activity from agent activity, and enforces real-time guardrails on what agents can do - with no persistent agent to install.

  • See it: a live entity graph of every user, agent, permission and credential across the fleet.

  • Know it: prompt-to-action attribution, activity timelines and continuous risk scoring.

  • Control it: a deterministic policy engine that returns Allow, Ask or Deny on the device in milliseconds.

Founded in 2025 and headquartered in Tel Aviv, Bay is led by Yuval Zacharia (CEO), Aner Morag (CPO) and Boris Danilovich (VP Engineering). Our engineers come from Mamram, Noname Security (acquired by Akamai), Waycare and other top Israeli cyber companies, and we already protect enterprise customers in the US.

The role

We're looking for a senior Account Executive to build and close Bay's enterprise pipeline in the US. You'll be one of our first sellers in the market, selling a new category - security for AI agents - to CISOs and security teams who are under pressure to adopt AI safely. You'll work closely with the founders, shape how we sell and help build the US go-to-market from the ground up.

What you'll do

  • Own the full sales cycle with enterprise and upper mid-market accounts, from first outreach to close.

  • Build your own pipeline through outbound prospecting, your network and events, alongside marketing and partner leads.

  • Run discovery, demos and proofs of value with CISOs, security leaders and practitioners, together with our Sales engineers.

  • Navigate complex buying processes - security, procurement and legal - and close new logos at a startup's pace.

  • Bring market feedback to product and the founders, and help define our sales playbook, messaging and process.

What we're looking for

  • 8+ years of enterprise B2B sales, with at least 5 years as a quota-carrying AE selling cybersecurity solutions.

  • A consistent track record of meeting and exceeding quota, year after year.

  • Experience at early-stage or growth-stage startups, ideally Israeli cyber startups, building a market rather than inheriting one.

  • A hunter: you create your own pipeline and don't wait for inbound leads.

  • A strong network of CISOs and security leaders in US enterprises.

  • Comfortable selling a new category: you can explain technical concepts like endpoints, identities and AI agents to both executives and practitioners.

  • Excellent communication, presentation and negotiation skills, and willingness to travel to customers and events.

Nice to have

  • Experience selling endpoint, identity, cloud or AI security products.

  • Experience as one of the first sales hires at a startup, or helping build a sales team.

Why join Bay

  • Sell a new category - security for the agentic era - at the moment every enterprise is deciding how to adopt AI agents.

  • Get in early: real enterprise customers are already live, and you'll shape how Bay sells in the US.

  • Work directly with founders and a senior team that has built and scaled security companies before.

  • Competitive base salary, uncapped commission and meaningful equity in a well-funded, seed-stage company.

  • Comprehensive health, dental and vision benefits.

Location: United States, remote, with travel to customers and events.

  • Work directly with founders and a senior team that has built and scaled security companies before.

  • Competitive base salary, variable compensation and meaningful equity in a well-funded, seed-stage company.

  • Comprehensive health and dental benefits.

jobs.title: Head of Research
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Bay

AI agents now write code, run commands and touch company data on employee laptops, in the browser, and in cloud sandboxes they spin up on demand. Bay is building the security layer that lets enterprises adopt them without losing control.

Bay is an agentic security platform. It discovers every AI agent, MCP server, IDE and browser extension across a company's endpoints and the cloud environments they connect to. It separates human activity from agent activity and enforces real-time guardrails on what agents can do, with no persistent agent to install.

Founded in 2025 by Yuval Zacharia (CEO), Aner Morag (CPO) and Boris Danilovich (VP Engineering), Bay has R&D in Tel Aviv and a growing go-to-market team in the US and Europe. Our team comes from Noname Security (acquired by Akamai), SentinelOne, Unit 8200, Mamram and other leading cyber companies, and we already protect enterprise customers in the US.

 

The role

We’re hiring our first Head of Research to lead and grow Bay’s research group and make it the reference point for how AI agents break and how to control them.

Today’s agents rarely live in one place. A desktop or browser client runs on the device, the model runs in the vendor’s cloud, and the work often happens in a remote VM or container. Your group will map that chain for every agent that matters: where actions execute, how commands travel, who is authenticated, and where Bay can observe or block.

You’ll lead the researchers already on the team, help grow it, stay hands-on with the hardest problems, and work closely with Aner Morag (CPO), detection engineering and R&D. Every project should make Bay’s product better and produce something worth publishing.

What you’ll do

  • Lead and grow the team: mentor the researchers already on board, take part in hiring new ones, and set how the group works, from target selection to evidence standards and disclosure.

  • Own the research agenda across coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot), cloud and computer-use agents, browser agents and extensions, and MCP servers. Decide what to research, in what order, and when to stop.

  • Stay hands-on: lead the deepest reverse engineering and vulnerability research yourself, across clients, runtimes and protocols on macOS, Windows and Linux.

  • Turn research into product: partner with product and R&D on interception points, enforcement primitives and threat insight, and make sure findings ship in Bay.

  • Run responsible disclosure for vulnerabilities such as sandbox and container escapes, cross-tenant access, credential exposure, prompt-injection-to-execution chains and tool or MCP abuse.

  • Be Bay’s research voice: publish blogs, CVEs, talks and open-source tools, and represent Bay at conferences, with customers and with the security community.

  • Build the research infrastructure, including tooling, labs and AI-assisted workflows (LLM-driven Frida, IDA or Ghidra over MCP), so a small team can move fast.

  • Keep Bay ahead of the threat: track new agent releases, agentic attacks and malicious packages, skills and extensions in the wild, and red-team Bay’s own guardrails.

What we’re looking for

  • A strong track record of original security research: vulnerabilities you found, disclosed or exploited (CVEs, bug bounty, vendor or red-team research). Usually 8+ years, but we care more about what you found than how long it took.

  • Experience leading researchers: you’ve hired, mentored or led a research team or group, and raised the quality of other people’s work.

  • Deep hands-on skills in reverse engineering (IDA, Ghidra, Binary Ninja or similar), dynamic instrumentation (Frida or similar), traffic interception and protocol analysis, including stripped binaries, certificate pinning and custom transports.

  • Strong OS internals: processes, IPC, sandboxing (namespaces, seccomp, micro-VMs) and networking. macOS is a plus.

  • Strong coding in Python plus at least one of TypeScript/JavaScript, Go, Rust or C/C++.

  • Product sense: you can turn a finding into something a product team can build, and you know which research moves the business.

  • Clear communication with engineers, executives, customers and the research community, in writing and on stage.

  • Fluency with AI agents as research tools, and the judgment to check what they tell you.

  • Evidence discipline: you keep what you observed and reproduced separate from what you inferred, and you hold the team to the same standard.

Nice to have

  • Research on LLM or AI security, prompt injection, agent sandboxes or software supply chain.

  • Cloud and container security: Kubernetes, container runtimes, cloud identity.

  • A public research profile: published research, conference talks (Black Hat, DEF CON, OffensiveCon or similar) or well-known open-source tools.

  • Experience building a research function at a startup or leading research at a security vendor.

  • Experience from a technology or intelligence unit (8200, 81, Mamram, Sapir or similar).

  • Exposure to detection engineering or threat hunting.

  • B.Sc. in Computer Science, Mathematics or a related field.

Why join Bay

  • Build Bay’s research group and set its agenda from the start, in a category that is still being defined.

  • Your findings ship in the product, with enterprise customers including Micron Technology, Peloton and ClickUp already live.

  • Work with the founders and a senior team that has built and scaled security companies before.

  • Competitive salary and meaningful equity in a well-funded, Series A stage company.

Location

Tel Aviv

‍

Bay is an equal opportunity employer. We welcome applicants of every background and don’t discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability or veteran status.

‍
